sentences.en: Hello and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the very unprofessional podcast whereby I, your unqualified guide,
sentences.zh: 你好，欢迎回到《20几岁的心理学》，这是一档非常不正经的播客，由我这个不合格的向导，

sentences.en: talk through some of the big changes and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 和大家一起探讨20几岁时的一些巨大变化与转型，以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: This week, we're discussing a pretty big buzzword in social psychology at the moment and over the past 10 years, FOMO, or fear of missing out.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们要讨论社交心理学中一个目前以及过去10年来非常热门的词汇：FOMO，也就是错失恐惧症。

sentences.en: So this term, it's risen pretty steadily in popularity within the past few years.
sentences.zh: 这个词在过去几年里知名度稳步上升。

sentences.en: And it's become a term I'm sure we all know pretty well and a feeling I'm sure we've all felt before as well.
sentences.zh: 它已经成了一个我们肯定都很熟悉的词，也是一种我们肯定也都体验过的感觉。

sentences.en: So FOMO refers to this overwhelming feeling of anxiety that an exciting or interesting event may currently be happening elsewhere and you're not invited, not included.
sentences.zh: 所以，FOMO指的是一种排山倒海般的焦虑感，觉得某个激动人心或有趣的事情现在正在别处发生，而你却没有被邀请、没有被包含在内。

sentences.en: It can often be aroused by, you know, your posts you see on social media or other forms of social triggers.
sentences.zh: 它常常会被你在社交媒体上看到的帖子或其他形式的社交触发因素所唤起。

sentences.en: So it's a sense that people elsewhere are having fun or doing things without you.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这是一种觉得别人在别处玩得很开心，或者在没有你的情况下做事情的感觉。

sentences.en: Pretty quickly, we can see how this has links to social anxiety and has a huge intersection with psychology despite being somewhat of a pop culture phrase in its current use.
sentences.zh: 我们很快就能看出这与社交焦虑有着怎样的联系，并且它与心理学有着巨大的交集，尽管它在目前的用法中多少算是一个流行文化短语。

sentences.en: But we're going to discuss some of the psychological underpinnings of FOMO, why it's so prominent in our 20s, possible remedies and its origins.
sentences.zh: 但我们要讨论FOMO的一些心理学基础、为什么它在我们的20几岁时如此突出、可能的应对方法及其起源。

sentences.en: We're also going to discuss how FOMO has been exacerbated by social media.
sentences.zh: 我们还将讨论社交媒体是如何加剧FOMO的。

sentences.en: So why social media is so harmful for our social and emotional wellbeing, its addictive properties as well, and how FOMO is part of that equation as well as being a consequence.
sentences.zh: 所以，为什么社交媒体对我们的社交和情感健康如此有害，它的成瘾特性是什么，以及FOMO如何既是其中的一部分，又是一种结果。

sentences.en: So let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 那我们开始吧。

sentences.en: So FOMO or the fear of missing out is a feeling or a state of mild anxiety.
sentences.zh: FOMO，也就是错失恐惧症，是一种轻度焦虑的感觉或状态。

sentences.en: I'm sure we've all felt at some point in our 20s, perhaps it's been stronger at times.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定我们在20几岁的某个时刻都感受过，有时这种感觉可能更强烈。

sentences.en: I think in this period of life, we are often surrounded by a lot of dense and varied social groups from uni, college to work, sports,
sentences.zh: 我认为在人生的这个阶段，我们周围往往环绕着许多紧密且各不相同的社交圈子，从大学、学院到工作、运动，

sentences.en: and we have pretty large extended social circles.
sentences.zh: 而且我们有着相当庞大的泛社交圈。

sentences.en: So it can be pretty difficult to feel comfortable in the amount you're socialising, especially with this ability to compare to others
sentences.zh: 因此，要想对自己的社交数量感到安心可能会相当困难，尤其是伴随着这种与他人进行比较的能力，

sentences.en: and whether people are doing things without you or you are being excluded.
sentences.zh: 去想别人是不是在背着你搞活动，或者你是不是被排挤了。

sentences.en: Our 20s, they are such a socially fast-paced and chaotic time, and we do feel that pressure to get the most out of our younger years and have those fun bonding moments
sentences.zh: 我们的20几岁是一个节奏极快且充满混乱的社交时期，我们确实感到了压力，想要充分利用我们年轻的那些年，去拥有那些快乐的凝聚时刻，

sentences.en: and experiences with friends that we can hopefully look back on later in life.
sentences.zh: 以及与朋友们的经历，希望以后在人生回望时能够有所回忆。

sentences.en: This is entirely a natural feeling.
sentences.zh: 这完全是一种自然的情感。

sentences.en: Wanting to be included and enjoy your life and be surrounded by people that you like and feel wanted by is normal, and it's also pretty healthy.
sentences.zh: 想要融入集体、享受生活、被自己喜欢的人包围并感受到被需要是正常的，而且这也是相当健康的。

sentences.en: We like the company of others and we enjoy being liked as well.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢有他人的陪伴，我们也同样享受被人喜欢的感觉。

sentences.en: So that's why that feeling that you are missing out on social experiences can be so daunting for many and create pretty intense feelings of insecurity,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么那种觉得自己错失了社交经历的感觉对许多人来说会如此令人生畏，并产生相当强烈的不安全感、

sentences.en: anxiety, self-doubt as well.
sentences.zh: 焦虑以及自我怀疑。

sentences.en: So I've kind of mentioned this already, but FOMO, it's not so much a scientific term, but more of like a cultural one at the moment.
sentences.zh: 我刚才其实已经提到过了，FOMO与其说是一个科学术语，不如说是目前的一个文化术语。

sentences.en: However, since we have been able to label it because these feelings have been around for many people in past generations, but with this label,
sentences.zh: 然而，自从我们能够给它贴上标签之后——因为这种感觉在过去几代人的许多人身上就已经存在了，但有了这个标签，

sentences.en: it has kind of become a source of research, particularly its undeniable links to social media and its ability to confront us with all the experiences we may be missing out on.
sentences.zh: 它在某种程度上已经成为了研究的课题，特别是它与社交媒体有着不可否认的联系，以及它能让我们直面所有我们可能错过的经历。

sentences.en: Maybe I think it's probably,
sentences.zh: 也许我觉得这可能……

sentences.en: I've kind of mentioned what FOMO is about, but it's probably good to define what it really means to begin.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚已经提到过FOMO是关于什么的了，但一开始也许最好还是定义一下它真正的含义。

sentences.en: So a recent study on the subject came up with a definition that has become somewhat standard in psychological communities.
sentences.zh: 关于这个主题最近的一项研究提出了一个定义，在心理学界已经变得有了一点标准性。

sentences.en: So it described FOMO as the uneasy and sometimes all-consuming feeling that you're missing out, that your peers are doing in the know about or in possession of more
sentences.zh: 因此，它将FOMO描述为一种不安的、有时甚至是全神贯注的感觉，觉得你正在错过，觉得你的同龄人知道得更多、

sentences.en: or something that's better than you.
sentences.zh: 或者拥有比你更多、比你更好的东西。

sentences.en: So under this framing of FOMO, this study concluded that nearly three quarters of young adults have experienced the phenomena.
sentences.zh: 在这种对FOMO的框架下，这项研究得出的结论是，近四分之三的年轻人都经历过这种现象。

sentences.en: So at least enough that they can actually recognise those nervous and anxious feelings, but I'm sure that statistic would be much higher if we also assessed people in contexts
sentences.zh: 所以，至少达到了能够真正识别出那些紧张和焦虑情绪的程度，但我敢如果我们也去评估那些写个人日记的人，或者更频繁地询问他们——比如一周一次甚至一个月一次——他们是否经历过FOMO，这个统计数据肯定会高得多。

sentences.en: when they kept personal journals or if they were asked more frequently, maybe once a week or even once a month, whether they had had an instance of FOMO.
sentences.zh: 因为这种被社交排斥和不安全感的感觉可能会让人非常难受，

sentences.en: Because this feeling of social exclusion and insecurity can be so uncomfortable,
sentences.zh: 我确信许多偶尔经历过的人可能都在压抑这种不适感，所以大概甚至不会意识到他们曾感受到那种不安，

sentences.en: I'm sure that many others who have occasionally experienced are likely suppressing the discomfort, so probably wouldn't even realise that they have felt that unease,
sentences.zh: 觉得自己错过了什么。

sentences.en: that they're missing out.
sentences.zh: 所以，错失恐惧症与轻度社交焦虑紧密相连，在患有广泛性焦虑障碍（即GAD）的人群中可能更常见。

sentences.en: So the fear of missing out, it's closely linked to a mild form of social anxiety and might be more common in those with generalised anxiety disorder, so GAD.
sentences.zh: FOMO伴随着自我意识过剩、不安以及对在社交场合中感到格格不入的担忧。

sentences.en: FOMO, it's accompanied by feelings of self-consciousness, of unease and concern about feeling socially out of place.
sentences.zh: 而这些都与某种特定形式的社交焦虑重合。

sentences.en: And these all overlap with a particular form of social anxiety.
sentences.zh: NPR的《隐藏的大脑》（The Hidden Brain）有一期非常棒的节目，如果你喜欢这些内容的话，那真是一个很棒的播客。

sentences.en: A really good episode by NPR's The Hidden Brain, which is a really good podcast if you are enjoying these.
sentences.zh: 但这个播客探讨了FOMO与社交焦虑之间的这种联系。

sentences.en: But this podcast, it discussed this link between FOMO and social anxiety.
sentences.zh: 因此，在他们的所有实验中，他们发现FOMO是一种特定焦虑的职能体现，即某种事情可能会在群体的经历中发生，

sentences.en: So in all their experiments, they found that FOMO is a function of a particular anxiety, that something might happen in a group experience
sentences.zh: 而这会塑造该群体未来的历史，这意味着你可能无法像你希望的那样融入那个群体，并且这会削弱你的群体归属感，

sentences.en: that will shape the group history in the future and that means you might not be a part of that group as much as you would like to be and it will undermine your group belongingness
sentences.zh: 这是因为在你不在场的情况下发生了一些情况。

sentences.en: because of something that's happened in the situation when you're not there.
sentences.zh: 因此，这可能会导致对未来情境的大量恐惧，在那些情境中，你可能会因为没有参加先前的那个社交活动而感到自己受到评判或孤立。

sentences.en: This can therefore contribute to a lot of fear of future situations in which you may feel judged or isolated because you didn't participate in that previous social event.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这表明了焦虑和FOMO是如何直接关系到人们对当前和未来社交环境的社会脆弱性的，在这些环境中，我们的确渴望被包容和接纳。

sentences.en: This shows, I think, how anxiety and FOMO are directly related to social vulnerability about current and future social settings and which we do crave to be included and accepted.
sentences.zh: FOMO并没有被收录在《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）中。

sentences.en: FOMO, it's not in the DSM.
sentences.zh: 所以DSM，我们之前讨论过，它是所有心理健康障碍最大的手册。

sentences.en: So the DSM, we've talked about this before, it's the largest manual of all mental health disorders.
sentences.zh: FOMO不在其中，但社交焦虑在。

sentences.en: FOMO isn't in there, but social anxiety is.
sentences.zh: 尽管我提到了它们可能是如何关联的，但它们是截然不同的，我认为不应该把它们混为一谈。

sentences.en: And although I've mentioned how they could be linked, they are distinct and I don't think they should be confused.
sentences.zh: 一方面，FOMO关注的是害怕被排斥在某个社交情境之外。

sentences.en: For one, FOMO concerns fear of being excluded from a social situation.
sentences.zh: 它是害怕不在那个社交情境中，因此可能包含一种趋向于过度社交的倾向，而社交焦虑

sentences.en: It's the fear of not being in that social situation and therefore maybe involves a tendency towards hyper and excessive socialization, whereas social anxiety
sentences.zh: 通常更多地涉及，你知道的，回避社交情境，或者害怕身处一个无法脱身的社交情境中。

sentences.en: is more commonly involves, you know, an avoidance of social situations or a fear of being in a social situation that you can't get out of.
sentences.zh: 但我们可以看出FOMO是如何促成社交焦虑的。

sentences.en: But we can kind of see how FOMO may contribute to social anxiety.
sentences.zh: 所以，患有社交焦虑（这是一种可诊断的障碍）的人对那些他们可能会被别人注视、评判、尴尬或拒绝的情境有着强烈的恐惧。

sentences.en: So people with social anxiety, which is a diagnosable disorder, they have an intense fear of situations where they could be watched, judged, embarrassed or rejected by others.
sentences.zh: 这些症状极其极端，以至于干扰了患者的日常生活，并阻碍他们参与普通活动。

sentences.en: And the symptoms are so extreme that they interfere with the person's daily routine and prevent them from taking part in ordinary activities.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，

sentences.en: In contrast,
sentences.zh: FOMO在专业意义上是不可诊断的。

sentences.en: FOMO is not diagnosable in a professional sense.
sentences.zh: 它还涉及害怕无法出席社交情境，而社交焦虑则涉及一旦我们身处其中就会爆发的那种恐惧。

sentences.en: It also concerns a fear of not being present in social situations, whereas social anxiety involves that fear that kicks in once we're in them.
sentences.zh: 因此，社交焦虑与这种错失恐惧症之间存在一些微弱的联系。

sentences.en: So there are some tenuous links between social anxiety and this fear of missing out.
sentences.zh: 它们都直接与人际关系以及我们心理中的社交元素相关。

sentences.en: They're both, you know, directly related to relationships and the social element of our psychology.
sentences.zh: 但FOMO似乎属于它自己的一类焦虑和不安。

sentences.en: But FOMO seems to be its own class of anxiety and unease.
sentences.zh: 在我们掌握如何将其减到最低之前，从心理学的角度了解它发生的原因是很重要的。

sentences.en: It's important to know why it occurs from a psychological perspective before we can grasp onto how to minimize it.
sentences.zh: 因此，让我们深入探讨可能的起因，以及相关文献对这种普遍的错失恐惧有什么说法。

sentences.en: So let's dive into the possible causes and what the literature says about this universal fear of missing out.
sentences.zh: 首先，许多理论假设FOMO源于预先存在的不安全感或不幸福感。

sentences.en: Firstly, many theories have hypothesized that FOMO emerges from a pre-existing insecurity or unhappiness.
sentences.zh: 那些在对能力、自主性和归属感的基本需求周围体验到较低满意度的人，往往会表现出更高水平的错失恐惧，

sentences.en: Those who are experiencing low levels of satisfaction around fundamental needs for competence, autonomy, and relatedness, they tend towards higher levels of fear of missing out,
sentences.zh: 那些总体情绪和整体生活满意度较低的人也是如此。

sentences.en: as do those who have lower levels of just general mood and overall life satisfaction.
sentences.zh: 确实显得FOMO的根源与其说是关于焦虑，不如说更多地与孤独感、低自尊、低自我同情有关。

sentences.en: It does appear that the root of FOMO is not so much about anxiety, but it's more to do with loneliness, low self-esteem, low self-compassion.
sentences.zh: 研究人员发现，如果你对自己的生活更满意，不仅仅是人际关系，那么你就不大可能经历FOMO，即使你面临着

sentences.en: If you're more satisfied with your life, not just your social relationships, researchers have found that you're less likely to have experiences of FOMO, even if you are confronted
sentences.zh: 自己可能正在错失某种经历或你希望被纳入其中的某事的想法时也是如此。

sentences.en: by the idea that you are potentially missing out on an experience or something you'd like to be included in.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上讲，我对它的理解是，与FOMO相关的情绪更多是个人生活中更深层不满的一种替代代理，

sentences.en: In that way, the kind of interpretation I have of that is that emotions associated with FOMO, they're more of a proxy for deeper dissatisfaction with one's life
sentences.zh: 而体验到“错失”的这种经历也可能只是起到了强化以往负面情绪和自我认知的作用，这也是为什么它会带来如此压倒性的、

sentences.en: and the experiencing of the experience of missing out may also just serve to reinforce previous negative emotions and self-perceptions, hence why it can be so overwhelmingly
sentences.zh: 总体上令人痛苦的体验。

sentences.en: and overall a distressing experience.
sentences.zh: 我研究的另一项有趣的探讨了人类如何看待“收益”与“损失”以作为FOMO解释的研究。

sentences.en: Another interesting study I looked into, it discussed how humans appreciate gains versus losses as an explanation for FOMO.
sentences.zh: 因此，研究表明，人们受损失的影响是受收益影响的两倍。

sentences.en: So research suggests that people are twice as affected by losses as they are gains.
sentences.zh: 所以这就说得通了，为什么我们的本能是去逃避错失的痛苦，并在我们确实经历失败时对这些失败耿耿于怀，这也说明了为什么这种感觉会比我们在社交或被接纳时实际获得的收益更强烈。

sentences.en: So it makes sense that our instinct is to avoid the pain of missing out and dwell on those defeats when we do and it also suggests why this feeling can be stronger
sentences.zh: 这也与更传统的进化视角联系在一起，该视角在某种程度上解释了为什么当我们无法享受我们想要陪伴的人的陪伴时，我们确实会感受到一种损失。

sentences.en: than the actual gains we get when we are socializing or we are included.
